description.short_caption: Chest CT scan showing cavitary lesion in the right lung.
description.detailed_description: This axial chest CT image shows a cavitary lesion in the right lung, with surrounding parenchymal changes. The lesion appears to have a thick wall and is located in the upper lobe. The mediastinal structures are visible, and there is no obvious pleural effusion. The scan is presented in lung window settings.
visible_findings: cavitary lesion in the right lung

Case_03056/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Figure 2. Gram stain of blood culture.

description.short_caption: Gram stain showing branching, filamentous bacteria in a blood culture.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Gram stain of a blood culture. The bacteria appear as branching, filamentous structures that stain purple, indicating they are Gram-positive. The background contains scattered cellular debris and other artifacts. The morphology is suggestive of an organism such as Nocardia or Actinomyces, though definitive identification would require further testing.

description.short_caption: Modified acid-fast stain showing branching filamentous organisms.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a modified acid-fast stain with pink-stained branching filamentous organisms against a lighter background. The organisms are consistent with the morphology of Nocardia species, which are partially acid-fast. The staining highlights the organisms' structure, aiding in their identification.
visible_findings: morphology consistent with partially acid-fast bacteria
